https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: Passenger on the plane appeals for help Israel What we know so far about alleged stabbing of pilot by co-pilot on flight to Israel Plane made emergency landing after pilot tried to crash aircraft, Israeli PM says, as officials investigate whether it was an attempted terror attack Tom Ambrose Wed 30 Sep 2026 11.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 12.43 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google One of the pilots of a plane flying from the UAE to Israel stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to try to crash the plane, the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, said, as Israeli officials said they were investigating whether the incident was an attempted terror attack on Israelis. Here is what we know so far: A commercial plane travelling from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Israel was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia , after an apparent brawl between its pilots prompted distress signals that briefly raised fears of an attempted hijacking. The flydubai flight was over Jordan when it diverted to Saudi Arabia, transmitting three emergency signals, one of which indicated a possible unlawful interference. The plane dipped dramatically during the reported fight, descending about 16,000ft in just two minutes. Israeli officials scrambled fighter jets, fearful of a possible hijacking attempt on a plane containing dozens of Israelis, and the plane landed at Tabuk airport in north-western Saudi Arabia. Graphic showing plane’s descent Netanyahu said one of the flydubai pilots stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to be intending to crash the plane. He added that a passenger managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members, and together they “neutralised” the attacking pilot. Netanyahu described it as “an extremely severe security incident”. Other officials, including the defence minister, Israel Katz, have called it an attempted terrorist attack. Netanyahu thanked the passengers and crew who helped to stop the attack, saying they “showed exceptional resourcefulness and courage”. An Israeli official has identified the attacker as an Omani national, Reuters reported. The Boeing 737 plane, which Israeli officials said had between 160 and 180 passengers onboard, transmitted a general emergency signal about two and a half hours after leaving Dubai , according to the flight-tracking website Flightradar24. Flightpath map A passenger on the flight, Miryam Shira Ohayon, said the plane was “pretty much out of control” when the alleged stabbing took place . “The co-pilot tried to murder the pilot and basically carry out a suicide attack on the plane,” she told reporters, on speakerphone held up by her mother, who was waiting at Ben Gurion airport near Tel Aviv. The plane transmitted the initial general emergency signal again before landing at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk airport. The airport said the plane landed at 9.45am local time and both pilots were taken to hospital after sustaining injuries. A second flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv landed safely at its destination. Flightradar24 initially showed flight FZ1081 diverting back towards the UAE but it was later shown to be on its way to Israel , where it landed in Tel Aviv on Wednesday afternoon. Photograph: Erin Clark/The Boston Globe via Getty Images Texas Amber Guyger, police officer who murdered black neighbor in his home, released from prison Guyger, convicted of murder of Botham Jean in Dallas in 2018, served seven years of 10-year sentence Marina Dunbar Fri 16 Oct 2026 13.45 EDT Last modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 14.58 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The former Dallas police officer who was convicted of murdering Botham Jean after entering his apartment and shooting him in 2018 was released from prison on Friday morning after spending seven years in prison. Amber Guyger, 38, regained her freedom a little more than two weeks after the Texas board of pardons and paroles approved her release , despite opposition from Jean’s family. The former officer was sentenced to 10 years in prison after her murder conviction on 1 October 2019. Her parole was approved exactly seven years after that verdict. The case against Guyger drew national attention after she fatally shot Jean, 26, inside his own Dallas apartment in September 2018. During her trial, Guyger maintained that she had accidentally parked on the fourth floor of the garage at the apartment complex where she and Jean lived. Jean’s apartment was located one floor above hers. Guyger testified that she believed she was entering her own residence when she walked into Jean’s apartment. According to her account, she attempted to unlock the door with her key when it pushed open. View image in fullscreen Amber Guyger testifies in court in September 2019. Photograph: Tom Fox/AP She claimed she mistook Jean for a burglar and fired her weapon because she feared for her life. Jean had been eating ice-cream and watching television in his apartment when Guyger entered and shot him dead. Guyger was taken into custody three days after the deadly shooting and was subsequently dismissed from the Dallas police department before standing trial. A jury found her guilty of murder. She faced a possible sentence of life imprisonment. Jurors ultimately gave her a 10-year prison term. Prosecutors had pushed for a minimum of 28 years, choosing that number to represent the age Jean would have reached at the time. Guyger first sought parole in 2024. But the parole board denied her request. When she became eligible to apply again, the board reversed course and granted her parole, allowing her to complete the remainder of her sentence under supervision. After the decision granting her parole, Jean’s family released a statement to CBS News Texas expressing their continued grief and requesting privacy. “Two days ago, the family of Botham Jean lovingly remembered their son and brother and celebrated his life on what would have been his birthday,” it read. “Today, it was reported that Amber Guyger will be paroled and will serve the remainder of her sentence under supervision. The family of Botham Jean respectfully requests privacy at this time as they process this development and continue to navigate their grief.” It continued: “To the many well-wishers who continue to say Botham’s name, honor his life, and carry his memory forward, the family extends their heartfelt gratitude for your continued love and support.” While Guyger’s release on Friday marks the end of her time in custody after the 2018 killing, she remains subject to supervision for the remainder of her sentence.
